question:
(a) Explain why the resistivity of a semiconductor decreases with increase in temperature.
(b) Compare this behaviour with that of a metallic conductor.

options.A:
(a) In semiconductors, rise in temperature creates more charge carriers, increasing conductivity; hence resistivity decreases.
(b) In metals, increased lattice vibrations cause more collisions, so resistivity increases. Thus semiconductors have negative and metals positive temperature coefficients.
options.B:
(a) Semiconductor resistivity increases with temperature because carrier concentration decreases.
(b) Metal resistivity decreases with temperature because collisions decrease.
options.C:
(a) Semiconductor resistivity remains constant with temperature.
(b) Metal resistivity remains constant with temperature.
options.D:
(a) Semiconductor resistivity increases because lattice vibrations increase.
(b) Metals have negative temperature coefficient due to increased free electrons.
